To further deepen student engagement and knowledge retention, the application 
will interleave questions that promote higher order thinking rather than mere 
fact regurgitation (Richmond & Hagan, 2011). To further bolster the applications 
engagement capabilities, gamified elements such as performance-contingent 
rewards and competitive elements will be investigated and utilised; finding new 
and innovative ways to cater to students’ needs. 
1.2 Aims and Objectives 
1.2.1 Aims 
• Develop an eLearning application to cater for the needs of GCSE 
students, that utilises short-form content delivery systems to enhance 
student engagement and content mastery. This application aims to 
deliver content in a way that aligns with modern social media 
consumption habits of students, with a particular focus on students 
influenced by the quick media intake rates on platforms such as TikTok. 
• Evaluate the effectiveness of integrating short-form content delivery  
combined with questions that promote higher-order thinking and gamified 
elements, at improving student engagement rates and content mastery 
within the context of GCSE subjects. 
1.2.2 Objectives 
• Conduct a comprehensive literature review to identify trends and gaps 
within eLearning frameworks and strategies; with a particular focus on 
short-form content, gamification, and other contemporary approaches. 
Additionally, this research will involve analysing existing research and 
theories related to cognitive load, attention spans, and digital learning 
methodologies. Standing as the theoretical foundation for the rest of the 
project.
